gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-pt-sans-caption: PT Sans Caption has big-bodied lowercase and bowls that feel open and inviting, a friendly plain sans for the running text. And Tilt Neon above it draws tube-like strokes of constant width, so the glow of the heading sits over a softer, more welcoming line.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-puritan: Tilt Neon lights up the top with a splayed c terminal and one tube-like stroke running through every glyph. Puritan follows in rounded forms with oversized e and a counters, a plain sans that stays friendly and easy on the eye.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-questrial: A splayed c terminal and tube-like strokes give Tilt Neon its glowing, sign-shop look. But Questrial is the one built for sustained reading, with open shapes and a flat, stencil-cut feel from a single weight.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-radio-canada: Tilt Neon's tube-like strokes never change width. Its large x-height and short ascenders make it earn its keep when set big and brief, while Radio Canada keeps to a sans-serif line with clear openings at every curve.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-radio-canada-big: Commanding in presence, Tilt Neon bends its tube-like strokes with a splayed c terminal and a large x-height. And Radio Canada Big runs a monoline plain sans whose terminals finish well clear of the stem, so a longer text moves along without snagging.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-readex-pro: Tilt Neon's tube-like stroke never changes width. That makes it a glowing showpiece for big, short words, while Readex Pro does the quiet work of a plain sans, with broad terminal gaps and a weight that holds steady word after word.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-roboto: Roboto has generous mouths on its round letters and little gap between capital and body height. Tilt Neon is the showoff here, its constant tube-like strokes and short ascenders made for display, while the sans-serif body handles the steady reading.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-ruda: Ruda brings a sizable x-height and a wire-like monoline skeleton, a sans made for screen reading. And Tilt Neon above it adds a splayed c terminal and tube-like strokes, so a loud heading sits over a slim, wide-mouthed body.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-saira: Tilt Neon glows with neon-tube strokes of constant width and a large x-height. Saira follows as a plain sans with rounded letters reaching high, though shrinking the heading would drain the tube effect that makes it work.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-sarpanch: Sarpanch opens its lowercase e clearly and keeps a compact gap between x-height and ascender line, a friendly sans for the text. Tilt Neon takes the top with bent-straw tube lines.
